selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search no longer escapes LIKE metacharacters

evidence.why: ns_condition now uses `store.prefix LIKE %s` with a raw namespace-derived pattern; `_` and `%` in namespace labels are interpreted as wildcards instead of literals, letting a namespace like `user_1` match unrelated namespaces such as `userX1`, weakening tenant isolation.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: Prefix/suffix match_conditions use unescaped LIKE and lost segment-boundary anchoring

evidence.why: The regex-based `_namespace_match_pattern` (anchored on `.` segment boundaries and escaped) was replaced by `prefix LIKE %s` built from unescaped `_namespace_to_text`, so `_`/`%` in a namespace label act as wildcards and prefixes no longer require a segment boundary (e.g. prefix `foo` now also matches `foobar`), allowing cross-namespace data to be returned from list_namespaces/search.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

findings.title: SQLite prefix search uses case-insensitive, unescaped LIKE

evidence.why: Replacing the GLOB-based `_namespace_prefix_condition` (escaped, case-sensitive, segment-anchored) with `s.prefix LIKE ?` on raw text reintroduces SQLite's case-insensitive ASCII LIKE matching and unescaped `_`/`%` wildcards, letting namespace `Foo` match `foo` and letting metacharacter-containing labels leak into unrelated namespaces' search results.

remediation.summary: Use parameter binding; never build SQL by string interpolation.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Upgrade now takes effect before request body is consumed

evidence.why: self._upgraded is set immediately when the Upgrade header is seen, and payload creation for Content-Length/chunked bodies is now skipped when upgraded, so a handler that declines the upgrade never gets the body read, and any request body bytes are left to be misinterpreted as the start of the upgraded protocol stream (HTTP request smuggling risk across the protocol switch).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: C parser upgrades immediately, skipping body read before switch

evidence.why: The deferred _pending_upgrade logic was removed and _upgraded is now set as soon as the Upgrade header is matched, before the request body (Content-Length/chunked) has been read, so leftover body bytes can be treated as upgraded-protocol data, enabling desync/smuggling between the HTTP layer and the upgraded protocol.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Removed symlink-clamped path resolution enables archive extraction path traversal

evidence.why: _safe_resolve was deleted and dest/parent are now built with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, rel_path); a crafted archive can plant a symlink (e.g. evil -> /) followed by an entry evil/passwd, and the write follows the symlink outside rootfs onto the host.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Hardlink source/dest no longer clamped inside rootfs

evidence.why: _defer_hardlink now stores raw os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_lparts) and dest without re-resolving through _safe_resolve at copy time, so a symlink planted earlier or later in the archive can redirect shutil.copy2's source or destination outside the rootfs.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Deferred hardlink copy no longer re-resolves paths at copy time

evidence.why: The loop now iterates raw (dest, src) tuples instead of re-resolving dest_parts/src_parts through _safe_resolve, so a symlink planted by a later member during extraction is not clamped before the copy2 call.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: _materialise_files loses symlink-clamped parent resolution

evidence.why: The function now computes host = os.path.join(rootfs_dir, arcname.lstrip('/')) directly instead of resolving parents via _safe_resolve, allowing an ADD'd tar or build stage to plant a symlink and write outside rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Restore no longer clamps destination through _safe_dest before writing

evidence.why: The call to _safe_dest(container_name, dest) was removed, so a backup archive with an earlier symlink member can redirect subsequent member writes outside the container directory onto the host filesystem.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Hardlink source in restore no longer clamped inside container

evidence.why: link_src is taken directly from _dest_path(member.linkname) without the removed _safe_dest(..., follow_final=True) resolution, letting a crafted linkname (or one routed through a planted symlink) cause shutil.copy2 to read an arbitrary host file into the rootfs.

findings.title: Path traversal / symlink guard removed from tar extraction

evidence.why: The safe_tar_extractall function with _is_within_directory checks for archive member paths and symlink/hardlink targets was deleted; extraction now calls tar.extractall() directly with only a mode-fixup wrapper, so a crafted tar (e.g. from a downloaded session) containing '../' paths or malicious symlinks can write files outside local_download_folder.

findings.title: Special/device file filtering removed from tar extraction

evidence.why: The prior guard rejected non-regular/dir/symlink members (e.g. device or FIFO files); the new code has no such check and forces all extracted files writable via forced chmod 0o200, restoring the CVE-2007-4559-style tarfile extraction vulnerability.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: Penelope unsafe tar extraction allows arbitrary local file write via crafted session archive

findings.title: Symlink-chain path traversal not fully prevented
